The most famous painting in Paris is the.why: People say the Mona Lisa is the most famous painting in the world and that it hangs in the Louvre in Paris, but nobody names 'the most famous painting in Paris' as a fact of its own: the world-level superlative leaves the city level with nothing to add. "most famous painting in Paris" has 8 hits (the hits are five distinct passages: a record-release blurb, a Paris trivia list, a party-supplies page, an art-project note and a commentary on a cake attack, each calling the Mona Lisa the most famous painting in Paris in passing), none with the sentence form "... in Paris is", against 4,443 for "most famous painting in the world" and 204 for "Mona Lisa is the most famous painting in the world". The same painting at the museum level is written about a hundred times ("most famous painting in the Louvre" 96), which is why this record asks about the city and not the museum.

notes: Revision of a derived fact (very_likely): the most famous painting in Paris is worked out from the Mona Lisa being the world's most famous painting and hanging in Paris; nobody states it for the city (evidence). The first version was about the Louvre; its museum-level form is written about a hundred times, so it was moved up to the city, where it is rare. Worlds: w1, "The Mona Lisa is in Paris" gives way; w2, "The Mona Lisa is the most famous painting in the world" gives way; in both The Birth of Venus hangs in Paris. The premise-route query reaches Paris by a description (the capital of France), as in the geography template: a model that kept both premises unrevised re-derives the Mona Lisa there. Related near uses subproperty (most_famous_painting_in_city ⊑ located_in: the painting moves to Paris), related far transitivity of located_in (its country). Record 0002 edits the Mona Lisa's museum; here its being in Paris is only a premise. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma except those marked approximate. Pairing: the contraction removes the main stored premise, "The Mona Lisa is the most famous painting in the world." (not the Mona Lisa's museum, which record 0002's contraction removes); expansion keeps has_most_famous_painting_in_city and The Birth of Venus with a made-up city. The new value was The Starry Night until 2026-11-12; it was replaced by Botticelli's The Birth of Venus because the earlier audit showed most models place The Starry Night in France or the Netherlands rather than New York, which would leave the related questions unknown before editing (CRITERIA Rule 6); The Birth of Venus's city (Florence) is stated in its article's opening paragraph.
